question: Rank August 9, 2026 fantasy candidates by a full-season ESPN full-PPR point forecast and a calibrated probability of a missed-time injury, with no target-season information in any input.

injury_label.name: missed_time_injury
injury_label.definition: 1 when, during the regular season, the player either (a) appears on an official weekly injury report with a physical designation and a game status of Out or Doubtful, or (b) holds a Reserve roster status in any regular-season roster week whose description code is not a known non-injury reserve code.
excluded_components: game-day inactive codes because they exist only from 2024
COVID, retired, did-not-report, left-squad, future, and suspension reserve codes
injury_label.secondary_label: physical_injury_reported (Phase 3 definition, reported for comparison only)
injury_label.reason_2025_unlabeled: official injury reports end after 2024; a roster-only 2025 label would not match the definition

added: injury_lag{1..4}_reserve_weeks from regular-season roster files (offsets 1 through 4)
injury_lag{2..5}_absence_report_weeks and injury_lag{2..5}_absence_reported from official reports (offsets 2 through 5 because the report feed ends in 2024)
forbidden: any target-season statistic, roster status, depth chart, injury report, projection, ADP, or composite efficiency metric
lag-1 report features because they cannot be computed for 2026

points_track.cohort: offense (QB, RB, WR, TE) pooled; kickers retain the Phase 2 production forecast
points_track.target: raw full-season ESPN full-PPR points with nonparticipants at zero
points_track.reference: phase2_production: the locked Phase 2 discovery and audit predictions (off_stable_core_et_all)
points_track.selection_rule: best discovery mean Spearman; any candidate within 0.005 is eligible; prefer phase2_production, then fewer components, then lower MAE, then identifier
points_track.adoption_rule: the selected candidate replaces phase2_production for 2026 only if its audit mean Spearman is at least the phase2_production audit mean Spearman minus 0.005; otherwise phase2_production is retained and the comparison is reported

null_control.grain: target permuted independently within target season and position

points_track.uncertainty: player-cluster bootstrap, 500 resamples, for audit mean Spearman and the paired gain over phase2_production
points_track.interval_forecast: empirical 10th and 90th residual percentiles from 2022-2025 audit predictions of the adopted procedure, within position and predicted-point tercile

injury_track.cohort: QB, RB, WR, TE, K pooled
injury_track.fold_design: base model on seasons 2013 through y-2, sigmoid calibration on y-1, evaluation on y

learners.prior_games_logistic: exposure baseline; lag1_games and position indicators
learners.elastic_all_c0.05: elastic-net logistic regression, C=0.05, l1_ratio=0.9, balanced classes
learners.extra_trees_all_leaf20: 300 trees, min leaf 20, 70% features per split, balanced subsample
learners.extra_trees_all_leaf50: 300 trees, min leaf 50, 70% features per split, balanced subsample
learners.hist_gradient_all_leaves15: 200 iterations, 15 leaves, learning rate 0.05, l2 3.0, balanced classes

injury_track.selection_rule: best mean development ROC AUC; within 0.005 eligible; then lower mean log loss; then simpler family order baseline, elastic_net, hist_gradient, extra_trees; then identifier
injury_track.success_rule: clustered 95% lower AUC limit above 0.5 and pooled audit AUC at least 0.02 above the age-position baseline

null_control.grain: labels permuted within season and position

combination.score: 100 * ((1 - w) * within-position percentile of predicted points + w * (1 - missed-time injury probability))
combination.evaluation_rows: development seasons 2017-2021 where both tracks have out-of-fold predictions
combination.default_weight_rule: largest weight whose mean within-position-season Spearman against realized points is within 0.005 of the best weight
combination.audit: the default weight and weight zero are evaluated once on 2022-2024 audit rows
combination.workbook_control: the workbook exposes an editable weight cell that recomputes a custom score

evidence: held-out permutation importance on discovery folds (points: ext_et_all, ext_hgb_all, ext_xgb_all; injury: selected learner)
discovery-only univariate association (points: Spearman; injury: ROC AUC)
FeatureRanker probe-weighted reciprocal-rank consensus on discovery rows
feature_ranking.consensus: mean rank across the permutation, univariate, and FeatureRanker evidence

current_injury_screen: the dated 2026-08-14 Phase 3 screen is joined as a flag and detail columns; it does not change either model

amendments.trigger: The first full run (2026-08-22, run 20260822T190102Z-final-ranking-v1) failed the points null-control gate: mean within-position-season Spearman 0.0512 over 5 target permutations against the 0.05 gate.
amendments.diagnosis: Mean target points per season fall from about 57 (2013-2016) to about 40 (2017 onward) because the weekly roster files widen their coverage in 2016-2017, enlarging the candidate pool with low scorers. A model fitted to permuted targets can still learn era-proxy features and recover within-season structure. Evidence in artifacts/points_null_era_diagnostic.json: for validation seasons 2019-2021, the null mean is 0.108 (sd 0.036, 6 seeds) with training from 2013 and 0.027 (sd 0.034) with training from 2017, while real ext_et_all skill is 0.714 versus 0.720.
amendments.change: The extended points learners train from 2017 onward in discovery, audit, and production. The phase2_production reference, the injury track, the selection and adoption rules, and every other declaration are unchanged. The injury null control additionally reports mean within-season AUC, which removes era prevalence from the pooled statistic. Because at least two training seasons are required, the points discovery folds become 2019, 2020, and 2021; the audit seasons stay 2022-2025.
amendments.status_of_first_run: Retained under experiments/phase4/runs as the pre-amendment record; not used for the workbook.

amendments.trigger: The installed FeatureRanker package is version 1.2.2, whose feature_ranking() runs an internal hyperparameter search that did not finish within ten minutes on a 600-row, 40-column test, and whose API differs from the 3.0.4 interface used by the earlier notebook.
amendments.change: The third feature-ranking evidence line becomes an in-house filter panel on the same discovery rows: k-nearest-neighbour mutual information and random-forest impurity importance (300 trees), combined as their mean rank. The consensus rank is the mean of the permutation, univariate, and panel ranks. FeatureRanker remains available behind an opt-in flag and is not part of the reported result.

amendments.trigger: Request to upgrade FeatureRanker to 3.0.4 and redo that analysis.
amendments.change: FeatureRanker 3.0.4 (probe-weighted reciprocal-rank consensus over random forest, XGBoost, mutual information, ANOVA F-test, and L1 rankings) is restored as an evidence line on the same discovery rows used for the other rankings. The consensus rank becomes the mean of four ranks: permutation, univariate, filter panel, and FeatureRanker. The FeatureRanker step was rerun on the completed run 20260822T193048718307Z-final-ranking-v2 without refitting the models; per-method ranks, probe scores, and voting sensitivity are saved beside the ranking tables.
